\cpara{The archived record bears this out. In December 1996 the author wrote on the Extropians mailing list that ``nanotechnology will turn the Earth into gray goo,'' and listed ``whether the Powers will be ethical'' among the ``post-Singularity'' problems for which ``All we need to know'' is ``Almost certainly'', ``of course'', and ``consider the alternative.''}
\cpara{Says that even after taking up Friendly AI, the author did not emotionally believe that failure was possible.}
\cpara{Ties the change to the insight told in ``My Naturalistic Awakening''.}
\cpara{The quoted sentence is the author's own, from the second virtue, relinquishment, in ``Twelve Virtues of Rationality''. The post does not say so.}
\cpara{A generalization about AGI researchers: being scooped and running out of money are real to them.}
\cpara{Contrasts, hedged (``I don't think''), the prospect of destroying humanity by their own mistake.}
\cpara{The post marks this as a guess about other people's minds (``It is unsafe to say'', ``it seems rather likely''). The support given is the next line: the author once said the same.}

\cpara{The author's 2001 document \textsc{Creating Friendly AI} bears this out. It argues that a controlled ascent should be ``fast enough not to give a significant speed advantage to a non-Friendliness-aware AI project.''}
\cpara{Says the author's childhood technophilia broke at that moment.}
\cpara{States the first lesson: following the rules of science, being a nice person, or being the best project available does not stop Nature from killing you.}

\cpara{The post's answer to the argument quoted above: rivals do not matter, since being the best project does not make a project safe. The post does not weigh whether stopping lowers the total risk while less careful projects go on, which is what that argument claims.}

\cpara{The archived writings bear this out. In January 1999 the author wrote that once nanotechnology could supply the hardware, ``a Singularity must be attempted immediately, before anything can go wrong.'' \textsc{Creating Friendly AI} (2001) argues: ``Thus, delaying FAI research will not make it any easier to develop Friendliness.''}

\cpara{\textsc{Creating Friendly AI} gives such reasons. It argues that mistakes would appear in order, many harmless ones before a catastrophic one, so that ``if no non-malicious mistake has ever been observed to cause catastrophic failure of Friendliness, the watchers can probably be fairly confident that none has ever occurred.''}
\cpara{Draws the lesson: good arguments for a risk do not stop the risk from killing you.}
\cpara{Restates the lesson with the gun image from earlier in the post.}
\cpara{Gives the reason as a general rule: without knowing the rules, you cannot model the penalty for not knowing them.}
\cpara{Applies the rule to other researchers, whose reply ``I do not know it cannot work'' the author calls wielding ignorance ``as a bludgeon.''}

\cpara{The post's rule: do not proceed until you ``know positively that the ground is safe.'' What would count as knowing positively is given two posts later, in ``My Bayesian Enlightenment'': doing ``only that which I understood on a sufficiently deep level to see that I could not do it in any other way.''}

\cpara{Dates the start of the author's training as a rationalist to this moment. In ``Something to Protect'' the author wrote: ``I only began to grow further as a rationalist once I had something terribly important that I needed to do.'' Here the start is the moment the author saw that the important thing could be lost.}
